hosted_note: 0180_card_payment_method_replacement_integrity.sql APPLIED to production 2026-08-13, DATABASE-FIRST, via `npx --yes supabase@2.102.0 db push --linked --yes` from a worktree checked out at the reviewed #562 head d0b4a311825f9a98a61b09726c61678982c46af7 (project alhhybgqdmcdyzpybykj), raw sha256 d5d8271da38588a89e0727ce7a2a5c417ee8e079ad283acdc1fa55f90727eb8d, executable sha256 160b39a7ad419438df96e240003bf814146e601dfeefc83bd5c1bbff23f5c4ea. CARD-ON-FILE REPLACEMENT INTEGRITY: card replacement becomes ONE transaction owned by the database. Adds the additive, SECURITY DEFINER, service_role-only command public.save_client_card_on_file(12 args) which re-validates customer and signature lineage, takes a same-mode advisory xact lock, retires the same-mode active card and inserts its replacement in the SAME transaction, so a failed insert rolls the retirement back and the previous active card survives. Before 0180 the retire and the insert were two separate PostgREST round trips, each its own transaction, which could leave a client with NO active card. APPLY EXIT STATUS: THE CLIENT PROCESS EXIT CODE WAS NOT CAPTURED. The `db push` process was terminated by the operator harness timeout before it returned, so no exit code exists and none is claimed. SERVER-SIDE COMMIT WAS PROVEN INDEPENDENTLY, and the proof does not depend on the client at all: the migration is a single begin;/commit; transaction whose only object statements are one CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION and one COMMENT ON FUNCTION, so partial application is impossible - it either committed whole or rolled back whole.
